steps.goal: Reach the upper/lower lanes, then use each role-specific latch to open the partner route.
steps.action: Ride or jump onto the marrow lift; Isp takes the blue upper route while Pac uses the lower platform, with the first available latch also restoring lift power.
steps.expected_feedback: The colored barriers stay role-specific; Isp blue opens Pac orange and Pac orange opens Isp blue.
steps.observed_feedback: Native ordinary-input trace reaches the upper route and later shows Isp at its exit while Pac is still travelling; both complete without deaths.

common_mistakes.recovery: Wait for the next powered phase or have either player latch a pad to restore power; reboard and continue.

confirmed: The visible room does require both color-matched exits and separates the heroes into different lane roles.
The screenshots exposed colored stay-on pads and a short glucose phrase; these are relevant to the powered lift and persistent latches.
First-pass uncertainty about the exact timing and recovery was warranted from idle-only evidence.
missed_mechanics: The lift is powered for 5 seconds and pauses for 3; it remains solid while paused.
Each hero’s latch both restores lift power and opens the other hero’s matching lane.
The two routes are reciprocal dependencies, not merely possible route assignments; both role-specific latch jobs are needed.
The room has no authored lethal hazards and has two optional role-specific collectibles.
incorrect_inferences: The first pass treated the five-second glucose text as a possible temporary route window. It refers to the lift’s powered phase; the paused lift stays solid and either latch restores power.
The first-pass prior record attributed Isp STOP and Pac RESCUE to level_04. Actual level_04 source/cues show Pac STEADY and Isp RESCUE; this correction is recorded here only.
changed_judgments: Reasoning rises from 3? The first-pass rating was 3; it stays 3 because actual reciprocal gates confirm the dependency anticipated from the split lanes, while the exact lift cycle adds detail.
Cooperation rises from 3 to 4 because each hero’s latch opens the other’s lane and both are needed, establishing repeated mutual dependence.
Timing changes from null to 1: a 5/3 lift cycle exists but its solid paused state and latch power restore remove a narrow mandatory window.
Hazards changes from null to 0 because there are no authored hazards; route proof also shows zero deaths.
Novelty rises from 2 to 3 because the exact combination of reciprocal gates and periodic marrow lift is new, though pads/ferries were introduced earlier.
Recovery cost changes from null to 1 because the solid pause and either power-restoring latch support a low-cost wait/reboard.
Solution clarity changes from 3 to 3; exact cycle and reciprocal effect are not fully explicit in idle cues, even though source and hint define them.
unresolved: The scripted route establishes feasibility, not how novices understand the marrow-lift cycle or coordinate the reciprocal gates.
The successful route evidence does not measure human recovery from a missed board or a wrong lane.
No actual player data establishes frustration, enjoyment, or co-op communication quality.

single_operator_note: A single operator must move both heroes through separated lanes and coordinate the two latches using WASD and arrow keys. The route can be advanced one hero at a time because the latches persist; this adds attention switching outside the two-human baseline.
